title: granularity='minutes' has no effect
body:
`timeparse(text, granularity="minutes")` in `pytimeparse/timeparse.py`
should read an ambiguous "H:MM" value as hours and minutes, as the
docstring shows, but it is still read as minutes and seconds:

```python
>>> timeparse("1:30", granularity="minutes")
90      # expected 5400
```

Expected: with `granularity="minutes"`, "1:30" is 5400 and "2:05" is
7500. Unambiguous inputs ("1:30:00", "1:30.5", "1h 30m") and the
default granularity are unchanged.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: The granularity check compares against a misspelled value.
